intended_object: The standard faithful (primitive) character of the cyclic group Z/4Z, k ↦ exp(2πik/4) = i^k, seen as an element of the Pontryagin dual of Z/4Z (written multiplicatively). This is read off the name "fourthRootCharacter" and the body; the docstring is only a generic placeholder.
explanation:
The body takes Mathlib's `ZMod.toCircle : AddChar (ZMod 4) Circle`, which sends j to exp(2πi·j/4). It turns this into a monoid hom on `Multiplicative (ZMod 4)` using `AddChar.toMonoidHomEquiv`. It then packages it as a continuous hom, i.e. an element of `PontryaginDual`. Continuity holds because the topology on the domain is discrete. So the result is exactly the character sending the generator to i. The library goes on to prove that it is injective, which is what one expects of the primitive fourth-root character.

This is one specific object, so the narrow setting is not a problem: the general construction is Mathlib's `ZMod.toCircle` for any n, and the definition just specializes it to n = 4 and repackages it as an element of the Pontryagin dual. I found no discrepancy.
